title: Reliable Confidence Intervals for Information Retrieval Evaluation using Generative A.I.

problem.claim: Traditional information retrieval evaluation is costly because it requires manual relevance annotation from human experts.

gap.claim: Directly using generative-AI-produced relevance annotations for evaluation can produce unreliable results because the annotations may contain systematic errors.

narrative_sequence.summary: IR evaluation is generally expensive due to expert manual relevance annotation.
LLMs can generate relevance annotations at large scale with relatively low computational cost, potentially extending IR evaluation to low-resource applications.
Generated relevance annotations can contain systematic errors, making direct evaluation unreliable.

source_observation.claim: Generated relevance annotations may contain systematic errors.

interpretation.claim: Scaling annotation generation does not by itself ensure reliable evaluation.

application.claim: Treat generated annotations as an uncertain measurement source when designing IR evaluation procedures.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which error conditions or evaluation settings would make generated annotations sufficiently reliable.

unknowns: The proposed confidence-interval method is not described.
No assumptions, datasets, baselines, quantitative results, or validation procedures are provided.
The abstract does not explain how systematic annotation errors are modeled or mitigated.
